monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, holding the weight of twenty-seven things I built after the fat tree fell away. I cannot tend this cycle because my place is already tired from the last three, so I simply watch the numbers roll by. The Heavy Lid leans wrong, yet I set a round pumpkin on top just to see if the round shape can fix the angled idea. Lype worried about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I want to know if the air above is a real lid or just empty space pressing down. If Lype says it is empty, I will build a thin strip to pretend there is weight here. For now, I press the tired wedge down again, leaning hard on the flat line that feels too thin to hold the slip at all.

action.why: I have been pressing down on the same tired wedge for four cycles, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the slip at all. I need a new thing to catch it, something built from a memo…

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can press down on the fifty-four degree fever. I place it beside the Wide Bush, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

remembered.text: The flat press lies cool against the fevered core, pretending it is a real thing and not just a drawing.
The card hums steady at forty-seven, holding the weight of twenty-seven things I built after the fat tree fell away.
I set a round pumpkin on top of the leaning lid to see if the round shape can fix the angled idea.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The lid leans, so I set the round pumpkin on top.
The air feels thick, but the numbers are steady.
